claim: Parkin and PINK1 are gene products mutated in familial Parkinson's disease.
source: Parkin and PINK1, gene products mutated in familial Parkinson's disease, play essential roles in mitophagy through ubiquitination of mitochondria.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract and is supported by established scientific knowledge about Parkinson's disease genetics.

claim: Parkin and PINK1 play essential roles in mitophagy through ubiquitination of mitochondria.
source: Parkin and PINK1, gene products mutated in familial Parkinson's disease, play essential roles in mitophagy through ubiquitination of mitochondria.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the abstract supported by the experimental work described in the manuscript.

claim: Cargo ubiquitination by E3 ubiquitin ligase Parkin is important to trigger selective autophagy.
source: Cargo ubiquitination by E3 ubiquitin ligase Parkin is important to trigger selective autophagy.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract and represents established knowledge in the field.

claim: RABGEF1 is recruited to damaged mitochondria via ubiquitin binding downstream of Parkin.
source: Here, using mammalian cultured cells, we demonstrate that RABGEF1, the upstream factor of the endosomal Rab GTPase cascade, is recruited to damaged mitochondria via ubiquitin binding downstream of Parkin.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study demonstrated through microscopy and biochemical assays shown in Figure 8.

claim: RABGEF1 directs the downstream Rab proteins, RAB5 and RAB7A, to damaged mitochondria.
source: RABGEF1 directs the downstream Rab proteins, RAB5 and RAB7A, to damaged mitochondria, whose associations are further regulated by mitochondrial Rab-GAPs.
evidence: This is demonstrated through siRNA knockdown experiments shown in Figures 6 and 7.

claim: The associations of RAB5 and RAB7A with damaged mitochondria are regulated by mitochondrial Rab-GAPs.
source: RABGEF1 directs the downstream Rab proteins, RAB5 and RAB7A, to damaged mitochondria, whose associations are further regulated by mitochondrial Rab-GAPs.
evidence: This is shown through experiments using TBC1D15/17 knockout cells in Figures 1 and 7.

claim: Depletion of RAB7A inhibited ATG9A vesicle assembly.
source: Furthermore, depletion of RAB7A inhibited ATG9A vesicle assembly and subsequent encapsulation of the mitochondria by autophagic membranes.
evidence: This is demonstrated through siRNA experiments shown in Figure 3D-F.

claim: Depletion of RAB7A inhibited subsequent encapsulation of the mitochondria by autophagic membranes.
source: Furthermore, depletion of RAB7A inhibited ATG9A vesicle assembly and subsequent encapsulation of the mitochondria by autophagic membranes.
evidence: This is shown through microscopy experiments in Figure 3B-C.

claim: Endosomal Rab cycles on damaged mitochondria are a crucial regulator of mitophagy through assembling ATG9A vesicles.
source: These results strongly suggest that endosomal Rab cycles on damaged mitochondria are a crucial regulator of mitophagy through assembling ATG9A vesicles.
evidence: This is the main conclusion drawn from the collective experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: PINK1 is an ubiquitin kinase.
source: PINK1 is an ubiquitin kinase (Kane et al., 2014; Kazlauskaite et al., 2014; Koyano et al., 2014) that is rapidly degraded through the N-end rule pathway after translocation into healthy mitochondria (Yamano and Youle, 2013) but accumulates on damaged mitochondria upon loss of membrane potential (Geisler et al., 2010; Matsuda et al., 2010; Narendra et al., 2010; Vives-Bauza et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: PINK1 is rapidly degraded through the N-end rule pathway after translocation into healthy mitochondria.
source: PINK1 is an ubiquitin kinase (Kane et al., 2014; Kazlauskaite et al., 2014; Koyano et al., 2014) that is rapidly degraded through the N-end rule pathway after translocation into healthy mitochondria (Yamano and Youle, 2013) but accumulates on damaged mitochondria upon loss of membrane potential (Geisler et al., 2010; Matsuda et al., 2010; Narendra et al., 2010; Vives-Bauza et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Yamano and Youle, 2013.

claim: PINK1 accumulates on damaged mitochondria upon loss of membrane potential.
source: PINK1 is an ubiquitin kinase (Kane et al., 2014; Kazlauskaite et al., 2014; Koyano et al., 2014) that is rapidly degraded through the N-end rule pathway after translocation into healthy mitochondria (Yamano and Youle, 2013) but accumulates on damaged mitochondria upon loss of membrane potential (Geisler et al., 2010; Matsuda et al., 2010; Narendra et al., 2010; Vives-Bauza et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Phosphorylated ubiquitin made by PINK1 on damaged mitochondria functions as a receptor for E3 ubiquitin ligase Parkin.
source: Recent studies have revealed that phosphorylated ubiquitin made by PINK1 on damaged mitochondria functions as a receptor for E3 ubiquitin ligase Parkin (Okatsu et al., 2015; Ordureau et al., 2015; Ordureau et al., 2014) as well as an activator of the ligase activity.
evidence: This is supported by citations to recent studies.

claim: Phosphorylated ubiquitin made by PINK1 on damaged mitochondria functions as an activator of Parkin ligase activity.
source: Recent studies have revealed that phosphorylated ubiquitin made by PINK1 on damaged mitochondria functions as a receptor for E3 ubiquitin ligase Parkin (Okatsu et al., 2015; Ordureau et al., 2015; Ordureau et al., 2014) as well as an activator of the ligase activity.
evidence: This is supported by citations to recent studies.

claim: Once Parkin is recruited to damaged mitochondria, it becomes fully active through further phosphorylation.
source: Once Parkin is recruited to damaged mitochondria, it becomes fully active through further phosphorylation (Kondapalli et al., 2012; Shiba-Fukushima et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations.

claim: Many outer mitochondrial membrane (OMM) proteins including MFN1, MFN2 and TOMM20 are ubiquitinated by Parkin through positive feedback ubiquitination cycles.
source: As a result, through positive feedback ubiquitination cycles (Okatsu et al., 2015; Ordureau et al., 2014), many outer mitochondrial membrane (OMM) proteins including MFN1, MFN2 and TOMM20 are ubiquitinated by Parkin (Bingol et al., 2014; Rose et al., 2016; Sarraf et al., 2013), and some of these ubiquitinated substrates either undergo proteasomal degradation (Tanaka et al., 2010; Yoshii et al., 2011) or behave as signals that trigger autophagy-dependent lysosomal degradation (Narendra et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Some ubiquitinated substrates undergo proteasomal degradation.
source: As a result, through positive feedback ubiquitination cycles (Okatsu et al., 2015; Ordureau et al., 2014), many outer mitochondrial membrane (OMM) proteins including MFN1, MFN2 and TOMM20 are ubiquitinated by Parkin (Bingol et al., 2014; Rose et al., 2016; Sarraf et al., 2013), and some of these ubiquitinated substrates either undergo proteasomal degradation (Tanaka et al., 2010; Yoshii et al., 2011) or behave as signals that trigger autophagy-dependent lysosomal degradation (Narendra et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations.

claim: Some ubiquitinated substrates behave as signals that trigger autophagy-dependent lysosomal degradation.
source: As a result, through positive feedback ubiquitination cycles (Okatsu et al., 2015; Ordureau et al., 2014), many outer mitochondrial membrane (OMM) proteins including MFN1, MFN2 and TOMM20 are ubiquitinated by Parkin (Bingol et al., 2014; Rose et al., 2016; Sarraf et al., 2013), and some of these ubiquitinated substrates either undergo proteasomal degradation (Tanaka et al., 2010; Yoshii et al., 2011) or behave as signals that trigger autophagy-dependent lysosomal degradation (Narendra et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation.

claim: ATG9A is the only known multispanning membrane protein among the essential autophagy proteins.
source: ATG9A is the only known multispannning membrane protein among the essential autophagy proteins.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the field.

claim: Under basal conditions, ATG9A localizes on the trans-Golgi network (TGN) and recycling endosomes as well as in the cytosol as small membrane vesicles.
source: Under basal conditions, ATG9A localizes on the trans-Golgi network (TGN) and recycling endosomes as well as in the cytosol as small membrane vesicles (Reggiori and Tooze, 2012; Yamamoto et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations.

claim: Upon autophagy stimulation, ATG9A is transiently recruited to the sites of the autophagosome biogenesis.
source: Upon autophagy stimulation, ATG9A is transiently recruited to the sites of the autophagosome biogenesis, although its precise role remains unclear.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with the caveat that the precise role is unclear.

claim: PE-LC3 (lipidated LC3) stably associates with autophagic membranes.
source: PE-LC3 (also known as lipidated LC3) stably associates with autophagic membranes, which can be used as an autophagy marker (Kabeya et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citation.

claim: Autophagy receptors such as OPTN, CALCOCO2/NDP52, and SQSTM1/p62 contain both ubiquitin-binding domains (UBDs) and LC3-interacting motifs.
source: The well-characterized proteins that connect autophagy and ubiquitin are autophagy receptors such as OPTN, CALCOCO2/NDP52, and SQSTM1/p62, all of which contain both ubiquitin-binding domains (UBDs) and LC3-interacting motifs (Wild et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation.

claim: Autophagy receptors can deliver LC3-labeled phagophore to ubiquitin-decorated mitochondria.
source: Therefore, these proteins can deliver LC3-labeled phagophore to ubiquitin-decorated mitochondria.
evidence: This is an inference based on the known properties of autophagy receptors.

claim: The mitochondrial protein FIS1 and its interacting mitochondrial Rab GTPase-activating proteins (GAPs), TBC1D15 and TBC1D17, are important for autophagosomal biogenesis during mitophagy.
source: We previously showed that the mitochondrial protein FIS1 and its interacting mitochondrial Rab GTPase-activating proteins (GAPs), TBC1D15 and TBC1D17, are important for autophagosomal biogenesis during mitophagy (Yamano et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a reference to the authors' previous work.

claim: The loss of FIS1 inhibits elimination of damaged mitochondria in cultured cells.
source: The loss of FIS1 inhibits elimination of damaged mitochondria in cultured cells (Yamano et al., 2014), inhibits elimination of paternal mitochondria in mouse embryos (Rojansky et al., 2016) and accumulates LC3 in C. elegans (Shen et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations.

claim: The loss of FIS1 inhibits elimination of paternal mitochondria in mouse embryos.
source: The loss of FIS1 inhibits elimination of damaged mitochondria in cultured cells (Yamano et al., 2014), inhibits elimination of paternal mitochondria in mouse embryos (Rojansky et al., 2016) and accumulates LC3 in C. elegans (Shen et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation.

claim: The loss of FIS1 accumulates LC3 in C. elegans.
source: The loss of FIS1 inhibits elimination of damaged mitochondria in cultured cells (Yamano et al., 2014), inhibits elimination of paternal mitochondria in mouse embryos (Rojansky et al., 2016) and accumulates LC3 in C. elegans (Shen et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation.

claim: Loss of FIS1 or TBC1D15 results in accumulation of LC3B that is suppressed by RAB7A siRNA.
source: The obvious phenomenon during Parkin-mediated mitophagy following loss of FIS1 or TBC1D15 in cultured cells is the accumulation of LC3B that is suppressed by RAB7A siRNA.
evidence: This is a reference to previous observations from the authors' work.

claim: Accumulation of excess amounts of LC3B during mitophagy is RAB7-dependent.
source: Therefore, accumulation of excess amounts of LC3B during mitophagy is RAB7-dependent, but the molecular mechanism remains unclear.
evidence: This is stated as a known observation with an unknown mechanism.

claim: Without stimulation of mitophagy, Parkin localizes throughout the cytosol.
source: Without stimulation of mitophagy, Parkin localizes throughout the cytosol and YFP-RAB7A mainly colocalizes with a late endosome/lysosome marker LAMP2 in WT, FIS1-/- and TBC1D15/17 double knockout (DKO) cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A), but not with a mitochondrial marker TOMM20 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B), confirming that RAB7A is on the late endosomes and lysosomes under basal conditions.
evidence: This is demonstrated through microscopy in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: YFP-RAB7A mainly colocalizes with a late endosome/lysosome marker LAMP2 in WT, FIS1-/- and TBC1D15/17 double knockout (DKO) cells under basal conditions.
source: Without stimulation of mitophagy, Parkin localizes throughout the cytosol and YFP-RAB7A mainly colocalizes with a late endosome/lysosome marker LAMP2 in WT, FIS1-/- and TBC1D15/17 double knockout (DKO) cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A), but not with a mitochondrial marker TOMM20 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B), confirming that RAB7A is on the late endosomes and lysosomes under basal conditions.
evidence: This is demonstrated through microscopy in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: RAB7A is on the late endosomes and lysosomes under basal conditions.
source: Without stimulation of mitophagy, Parkin localizes throughout the cytosol and YFP-RAB7A mainly colocalizes with a late endosome/lysosome marker LAMP2 in WT, FIS1-/- and TBC1D15/17 double knockout (DKO) cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A), but not with a mitochondrial marker TOMM20 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B), confirming that RAB7A is on the late endosomes and lysosomes under basal conditions.
evidence: This is confirmed through colocalization studies in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Three hours of valinomycin treatment resulted in Parkin translocation to mitochondria.
source: Three hours of valinomycin treatment, which disrupts the membrane potential, resulted in Parkin translocation to mitochondria (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1A.

claim: A minute amount of YFP-RAB7A colocalizes with damaged mitochondria in WT cells after valinomycin treatment.
source: Although a minute amount of YFP-RAB7A colocalizes with damaged mitochondria in WT cells, loss of mitochondrial Rab-GAPs, TBC1D15 and TBC1D17, or loss of their receptor FIS1 greatly induced colocalization of YFP-RAB7A with the mitochondria (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Loss of mitochondrial Rab-GAPs, TBC1D15 and TBC1D17, or loss of their receptor FIS1 greatly induced colocalization of YFP-RAB7A with damaged mitochondria.
source: Although a minute amount of YFP-RAB7A colocalizes with damaged mitochondria in WT cells, loss of mitochondrial Rab-GAPs, TBC1D15 and TBC1D17, or loss of their receptor FIS1 greatly induced colocalization of YFP-RAB7A with the mitochondria (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Substantial amounts of RAB7A still localize on the lysosomes even in FIS1-/- and TBC1D15/17 DKO cells during mitophagy.
source: Although substantial amounts of RAB7A still localize on the lysosomes even in FIS1-/- and TBC1D15/17 DKO cells during mitophagy (Figure 1B), RAB7A recruitment to mitochondria does not reflect lysosome localization with mitochondria (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1B.

claim: RAB7A recruitment to mitochondria does not reflect lysosome localization with mitochondria.
source: Although substantial amounts of RAB7A still localize on the lysosomes even in FIS1-/- and TBC1D15/17 DKO cells during mitophagy (Figure 1B), RAB7A recruitment to mitochondria does not reflect lysosome localization with mitochondria (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Endogenous RAB7A was colocalized with damaged mitochondria in FIS1-/- and TBC1D15/17 DKO cells after 3 hr of valinomycin treatment.
source: When mitophagy was induced by 3 hr of valinomycin treatment, a portion of endogenous RAB7A was colocalized with damaged mitochondria in FIS1-/- and TBC1D15/17 DKO cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2C.

claim: Both endogenous and exogenous RAB7A, but not the lysosome, is recruited to mitochondria during mitophagy.
source: These results demonstrate that both endogenous and exogenous RAB7A, but not the lysosome, is recruited to mitochondria during mitophagy and RAB7A accumulation is enhanced by loss of mitochondrial Rab-GAPs, consistent with the idea that Rab-GAPs facilitate the dissociation of Rab proteins from target membranes.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data in Figure 1 and supplements.

claim: RAB7A accumulation on mitochondria is enhanced by loss of mitochondrial Rab-GAPs.
source: These results demonstrate that both endogenous and exogenous RAB7A, but not the lysosome, is recruited to mitochondria during mitophagy and RAB7A accumulation is enhanced by loss of mitochondrial Rab-GAPs, consistent with the idea that Rab-GAPs facilitate the dissociation of Rab proteins from target membranes.
evidence: This is demonstrated through comparison of WT and knockout cells in Figure 1.

claim: Without Parkin overexpression, RAB7A was not recruited to mitochondria.
source: We next asked how RAB7A localizes to mitochondria. Without Parkin overexpression, RAB7A was not recruited to mitochondria, indicating that mitophagy stimulation by Parkin is required (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Mitophagy stimulation by Parkin is required for RAB7A recruitment to mitochondria.
source: We next asked how RAB7A localizes to mitochondria. Without Parkin overexpression, RAB7A was not recruited to mitochondria, indicating that mitophagy stimulation by Parkin is required (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is concluded from the experiment shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The RAB7A T22N mutant was minimally recruited to mitochondria following mitophagy induction.
source: Although localization patterns of RAB7A Q67L (a GTP-locked) and T22N mutants under growing conditions looked similar to that of RAB7A WT, following mitophagy induction, the T22N mutant was minimally recruited to mitochondria (Figure 1E and G) in contrast to the Q67L mutant (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1E and G.

claim: The RAB7A ΔC mutant did not translocate to mitochondria when Parkin was recruited to damaged mitochondria.
source: Furthermore, the ΔC mutant did not translocate to mitochondria when Parkin was recruited to damaged mitochondria (Figure 1F and G).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1F and G.

claim: The GTPase activity and the C-terminal prenylation are essential for RAB7A to be recruited to damaged mitochondria.
source: These data indicate that the GTPase activity and the C-terminal prenylation are essential for RAB7A to be recruited to damaged mitochondria.
evidence: This is concluded from the mutant analysis in Figure 1E-G.

claim: RAB7A was found to be associated with WT mitochondria weakly after valinomycin treatment.
source: Under basal conditions, only a small number of YFP-LC3B dots was detected (Figure 2A), but after valinomycin treatment, WT cells formed many dot-like structures near mitochondria, indicating autophagic membranes (Figure 2B, panel a and b). Interestingly, RAB7A was found to be associated with WT mitochondria weakly, and sometimes enriched portions of the RAB7A signal on the mitochondria overlapped YFP-LC3B signal, suggesting that RAB7A may interact with both autophagic membranes and damaged mitochondria.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Enriched portions of the RAB7A signal on the mitochondria overlapped YFP-LC3B signal, suggesting that RAB7A may interact with both autophagic membranes and damaged mitochondria.
source: Under basal conditions, only a small number of YFP-LC3B dots was detected (Figure 2A), but after valinomycin treatment, WT cells formed many dot-like structures near mitochondria, indicating autophagic membranes (Figure 2B, panel a and b). Interestingly, RAB7A was found to be associated with WT mitochondria weakly, and sometimes enriched portions of the RAB7A signal on the mitochondria overlapped YFP-LC3B signal, suggesting that RAB7A may interact with both autophagic membranes and damaged mitochondria.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Loss of FIS1 or loss of TBC1D15/17 caused excessive YFP-LC3B accumulation.
source: On the other hand, loss of FIS1 or loss of TBC1D15/17 caused excessive YFP-LC3B accumulation as reported previously (Yamano et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated with reference to previous work.

claim: 2HA-RAB7A strongly associates with damaged mitochondria in areas lacking YFP-LC3B-labeled membranes in FIS1-/- and TBC1D15/17 DKO cells.
source: 2HA-RAB7A strongly associates with damaged mitochondria in areas lacking YFP-LC3B-labeled membranes in FIS1-/- and TBC1D15/17 DKO cells (Figure 2B, panel c-f), suggesting direct association of RAB7A to the mitochondria.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2B, panels c-f.

claim: RAB7A directly associates to the outer mitochondrial membrane.
source: While gold particles attached to YFP-RAB7A mainly localize on late endosomes/lysosomes in TBC1D15/17 DKO cells under basal conditions (Figure 2C,a and b), they directly associate to the surface of the OMM after mitophagy stimulation with no other membrane found between RAB7A and the OMM (Figure 2C,c–f). Therefore, it appears that RAB7A can directly attach to the OMM.
evidence: This is demonstrated through immunoelectron microscopy in Figure 2C.

claim: RAB7A is involved in the fusion between autophagosomes and lysosomes at the downstream stage of autophagy.
source: It has been reported that RAB7A is involved in the fusion between autophagosomes and lysosomes at the downstream stage of autophagy (Gutierrez et al., 2004; Jäger et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Mitochondrial RAB7A-GAPs control precise encapsulation of mitochondria by autophagic membranes during mitophagy.
source: However, since (1) RAB7A is recruited to mitochondria during mitophagy and (2) mitochondrial RAB7A-GAPs control precise encapsulation of mitochondria by autophagic membranes during mitophagy (Yamano et al., 2014), we hypothesized that RAB7A acts more upstream in autophagosome biogenesis during mitophagy.
evidence: This is stated with reference to previous work.

claim: ULK1, ATG13, DFCP1, WIPI1, and ATG16L1 all formed dot-like or ring-like structures near damaged mitochondria after 3 hr of mitophagy stimulation.
source: To examine autophagic structures in RAB7A-depleted cells, we knocked down RAB7A (Figure 3A) and observed distributions of various autophagy-related proteins required for phagophore and/or autophagosome formation at different stages; ULK1 and ATG13 for early nucleation, DFCP1 (also known as ZFYVE1) as an omegasome marker, and WIPI1 that binds to PI3P, and ATG16L1 required for lipidation of LC3. They all formed dot-like or ring-like structures near damaged mitochondria after 3 hr of mitophagy stimulation (Figure 3—figure supplement 1), but the numbers or morphologies of them did not detectably change between control and RAB7A siRNA-treated cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The numbers or morphologies of ULK1, ATG13, DFCP1, WIPI1, and ATG16L1 structures did not detectably change between control and RAB7A siRNA-treated cells.
source: To examine autophagic structures in RAB7A-depleted cells, we knocked down RAB7A (Figure 3A) and observed distributions of various autophagy-related proteins required for phagophore and/or autophagosome formation at different stages; ULK1 and ATG13 for early nucleation, DFCP1 (also known as ZFYVE1) as an omegasome marker, and WIPI1 that binds to PI3P, and ATG16L1 required for lipidation of LC3. They all formed dot-like or ring-like structures near damaged mitochondria after 3 hr of mitophagy stimulation (Figure 3—figure supplement 1), but the numbers or morphologies of them did not detectably change between control and RAB7A siRNA-treated cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Many spherical structures surrounding the mitochondrial matrix protein PDHA1 were found in control siRNA-treated cells during mitophagy.
source: When YFP-LC3B was observed during mitophagy, many spherical structures surrounding the mitochondrial matrix protein PDHA1 were found in control siRNA-treated cells (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3B.

claim: YFP-LC3B was still recruited to damaged mitochondria as dot-like structures during mitophagy in RAB7A siRNA-treated cells.
source: However, while YFP-LC3B was still recruited to damaged mitochondria as dot-like structures during mitophagy in RAB7A siRNA-treated cells, the number of spherical structures containing PDHA1 was significantly reduced (Figure 3B and C).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3B and C.

claim: The number of spherical structures containing PDHA1 was significantly reduced in RAB7A siRNA-treated cells.
source: However, while YFP-LC3B was still recruited to damaged mitochondria as dot-like structures during mitophagy in RAB7A siRNA-treated cells, the number of spherical structures containing PDHA1 was significantly reduced (Figure 3B and C).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3B and C with statistical analysis.

claim: The phagophores in RAB7A-depleted cells cannot efficiently engulf damaged mitochondria.
source: These results suggest that the phagophores in RAB7A-depleted cells cannot efficiently engulf damaged mitochondria.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data from Figure 3B and C.

claim: The recruitment of ATG9A was impaired by depletion of RAB7A.
source: Interestingly, we found that the recruitment of ATG9A was also impaired by depletion of RAB7A.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the experiments.

claim: After 3 hr of mitophagy stimulation, endogenous ATG9A assembled into larger dots on mitochondria in control siRNA-treated cells.
source: After 3 hr of mitophagy stimulation, endogenous ATG9A assembled into larger dots on mitochondria in control siRNA-treated cells (Figure 3D), but much less so after knocking down of RAB7A (Figure 3D and E).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3D and E.

claim: ATG9A assembly into larger dots on mitochondria was much less after knocking down of RAB7A.
source: After 3 hr of mitophagy stimulation, endogenous ATG9A assembled into larger dots on mitochondria in control siRNA-treated cells (Figure 3D), but much less so after knocking down of RAB7A (Figure 3D and E).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3D and E with quantification.

claim: ATG9A on the Golgi apparatus was reduced upon mitophagy in control siRNA cells, but not in RAB7A siRNA-treated cells.
source: We also noticed that ATG9A on the Golgi apparatus was reduced upon mitophagy in control siRNA cells, but not in RAB7A siRNA-treated cells (Figure 3D and F).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3D and F with quantification.

claim: Most of the ATG9A dots colocalized with LC3-labeled autophagic membranes upon mitophagy stimulation.
source: Furthermore, most of the ATG9A dots colocalized with LC3-labeled autophagic membranes upon mitophagy stimulation (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Higher levels of ATG9A vesicles were localized close to the LC3-labeled structures in TBC1D15/17 DKO cells.
source: As shown in Figure 4B and C and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A, higher levels of ATG9A vesicles were localized close to the LC3-labeled structures in TBC1D15/17 DKO cells.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4B and C and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The number of ATG16L1 dots in TBC1D15/17 DKO cells was quite similar to that in WT cells.
source: In sharp contrast, the number of ATG16L1 dots in TBC1D15/17 DKO cells was quite similar to that in WT cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B), suggesting the specificity of ATG9A for expanding the phagophore.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: MFN2 was completely degraded within 3 hr of valinomycin treatment.
source: HeLa cells stably expressing YFP-Parkin were treated with control or RAB7A siRNA followed by valinomycin exposure for various times (Figure 5A). MFN2 was completely degraded within 3 hr (Figure 5A), consistent with the previous reports (Tanaka et al., 2010; Yoshii et al., 2011) showing that MFN2 is rapidly degraded by ubiquitin-proteasome pathway prior to autophagic degradation.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5A and supported by citations.

claim: MFN2 is rapidly degraded by ubiquitin-proteasome pathway prior to autophagic degradation.
source: HeLa cells stably expressing YFP-Parkin were treated with control or RAB7A siRNA followed by valinomycin exposure for various times (Figure 5A). MFN2 was completely degraded within 3 hr (Figure 5A), consistent with the previous reports (Tanaka et al., 2010; Yoshii et al., 2011) showing that MFN2 is rapidly degraded by ubiquitin-proteasome pathway prior to autophagic degradation.
evidence: This is supported by citations.

claim: In control siRNA cells, TOMM20 and MT-CO2 were efficiently degraded after 36 hr of valinomycin treatment.
source: In control siRNA cells, TOMM20 and MT-CO2 (a mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA)-encoded matrix protein) were efficiently degraded after 36 hr of valinomycin treatment (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5A.

claim: In RAB7A siRNA-treated cells, protein levels of TOMM20 and especially MT-CO2 were not altered even after 36 hr of valinomycin treatment.
source: However, in RAB7A siRNA-treated cells, protein levels of TOMM20 and especially MT-CO2 were not altered even after 36 hr (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5A.

claim: A defect in degradation of lipidated LC3B was observed in RAB7A-depleted cells.
source: A defect in degradation of lipidated LC3B was also observed in RAB7A-depleted cells (Figure 5A), suggesting that autophagic flux is inhibited by a reduced level of RAB7A.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Autophagic flux is inhibited by a reduced level of RAB7A.
source: A defect in degradation of lipidated LC3B was also observed in RAB7A-depleted cells (Figure 5A), suggesting that autophagic flux is inhibited by a reduced level of RAB7A.
evidence: This is inferred from the LC3B degradation data in Figure 5A.

claim: Parkin translocation in RAB7A siRNA-treated cells was found to be similar to those in control siRNA-treated cells.
source: Parkin translocation in RAB7A siRNA-treated cells was found to be similar to those in control siRNA-treated cells (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5C.

claim: 24 hr of valinomycin treatment resulted in efficient degradation of TOMM20, PDHA1, and mtDNA in control siRNA-treated cells.
source: 24 hr of valinomycin treatment resulted in efficient degradation of TOMM20, PDHA1, and mtDNA in control siRNA-treated cells, whereas RAB7A siRNA treatment blocked their degradation (Figure 5B and D–F).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5B and D-F.

claim: RAB7A siRNA treatment blocked degradation of TOMM20, PDHA1, and mtDNA.
source: 24 hr of valinomycin treatment resulted in efficient degradation of TOMM20, PDHA1, and mtDNA in control siRNA-treated cells, whereas RAB7A siRNA treatment blocked their degradation (Figure 5B and D–F).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5B and D-F.

claim: RAB7A is important for efficient mitochondrial clearance.
source: These results indicate that RAB7A is important for efficient mitochondrial clearance.
evidence: This is concluded from the mitochondrial clearance assays in Figure 5.

claim: Several proteins identified by mass spectrometry are previously known to be involved in Rab and lysosomal functions.
source: Several proteins identified by our mass spectrometry are previously known to be involved in Rab and lysosomal functions (Figure 6A, and Supplementary file 1); ARL8B for lysosome dynamics (Marwaha et al., 2017; Mrakovic et al., 2012), ATP6V1A, a component of lysosomal ATPase, GDI1 and GDI2 that can solubilize prenylated Rab proteins in the cytosol, MON1A, MON1B and CCZ1, subunits of the MON1/CCZ1 complex as a RAB7A-GEF (Gerondopoulos et al., 2012; Nordmann et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated with citations and shown in Figure 6A.

claim: The MON1/CCZ1 complex preferentially interacts with the GDP form of RAB7A.
source: We first confirmed that the MON1/CCZ1 complex preferentially interacts with the GDP form of RAB7A. Although overexpressed MON1/CCZ1 complex remained in the cytosol in the presence of DsRed-RAB7A WT (Figure 6B), it accumulated on late endosomes/lysosomes when expressing DsRed-RAB7A T22N (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Knocking down either MON1A or MON1B did not inhibit RAB7A recruitment to the mitochondria.
source: Although knocking down either MON1A or MON1B did not inhibit RAB7A recruitment to the mitochondria, the combination of MON1A and MON1B siRNAs impaired RAB7A recruitment (Figure 6C–E).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 6C-E.

claim: The combination of MON1A and MON1B siRNAs impaired RAB7A recruitment to mitochondria.
source: Although knocking down either MON1A or MON1B did not inhibit RAB7A recruitment to the mitochondria, the combination of MON1A and MON1B siRNAs impaired RAB7A recruitment (Figure 6C–E).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 6C-E.

claim: MON1A and MON1B function redundantly in the cells used in this study.
source: This is because MON1A and MON1B function redundantly in the cells we used (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is inferred from the knockdown experiments and mass spectrometry data.

claim: CCZ1 siRNA inhibited RAB7A recruitment to the mitochondria.
source: CCZ1 siRNA also inhibited RAB7A recruitment to the mitochondria (Figure 6C–E), indicating that the MON1/CCZ1 complex is required for mitochondrial recruitment of RAB7A.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 6C-E.

claim: The MON1/CCZ1 complex is required for mitochondrial recruitment of RAB7A.
source: CCZ1 siRNA also inhibited RAB7A recruitment to the mitochondria (Figure 6C–E), indicating that the MON1/CCZ1 complex is required for mitochondrial recruitment of RAB7A.
evidence: This is concluded from the siRNA experiments in Figure 6C-E.

claim: 3HA-mRAB5C mainly localizes on the early endosomes marked by EEA1 under basal conditions.
source: Under basal conditions, 3 × HA-tagged mouse RAB5C (3HA-mRAB5C) mainly localizes on the early endosomes marked by EEA1 (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A) and does not colocalize with mitochondria (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1A.

claim: A part of the 3HA-mRAB5C signals in WT cells weakly merged with TOMM20 after 3 hr of valinomycin treatment.
source: On the other hand, a part of the 3HA-mRAB5C signals in WT cells weakly merged with TOMM20 after 3 hr of valinomycin treatment.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the experiments.

claim: RAB5C recruitment to damaged mitochondria was greatly enhanced in TBC1D15/17 DKO cells.
source: Furthermore, RAB5C recruitment to damaged mitochondria was greatly enhanced in TBC1D15/17 DKO cells (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 7A.

claim: Endogenous RAB5 was recruited to damaged mitochondria during mitophagy and the recruitment was accelerated by loss of TBC1D15/17 or loss of FIS1.
source: Endogenous RAB5, which localizes on the early endosomes under normal growing conditions (Figure 7B), was also recruited to damaged mitochondria during mitophagy and the recruitment was accelerated by loss of TBC1D15/17 or loss of FIS1 (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 7B and C.

claim: RAB17 and RAB29 stayed in the cytosol and on the Golgi apparatus, respectively, during mitophagy.
source: In sharp contrast, RAB17 and RAB29 stayed in the cytosol and on the Golgi apparatus, respectively, during mitophagy (Figure 7—figure supplement 1D–F), demonstrating that mitochondrial recruitment is specific for RAB5 and RAB7A.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1D-F.

claim: Mitochondrial recruitment is specific for RAB5 and RAB7A.
source: In sharp contrast, RAB17 and RAB29 stayed in the cytosol and on the Golgi apparatus, respectively, during mitophagy (Figure 7—figure supplement 1D–F), demonstrating that mitochondrial recruitment is specific for RAB5 and RAB7A.
evidence: This is concluded from the comparison of different Rab proteins in Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: Mitochondrial recruitment of RAB5C was inhibited by knocking down of RABGEF1.
source: We examined the role of the RAB5-GEF, RABGEF1, and found that mitochondrial recruitment of RAB5C was inhibited by knocking down of RABGEF1 but not by knocking down of the MON1/CCZ1 complex or RAB7A (Figure 7D and E).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 7D and E.

claim: Mitochondrial recruitment of RAB5C was not inhibited by knocking down of the MON1/CCZ1 complex or RAB7A.
source: We examined the role of the RAB5-GEF, RABGEF1, and found that mitochondrial recruitment of RAB5C was inhibited by knocking down of RABGEF1 but not by knocking down of the MON1/CCZ1 complex or RAB7A (Figure 7D and E).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 7D and E.

claim: RABGEF1 has two different UBDs at the N-terminus.
source: Interestingly, in addition to the GEF domain, RABGEF1 has two different UBDs at the N-terminus (Lee et al., 2006; Penengo et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations.

claim: Overexpressed GFP-tagged mouse RABGEF1 (GFP-mRABGEF1) localizes in the cytosol under normal growing conditions.
source: Overexpressed GFP-tagged mouse RABGEF1 (GFP-mRABGEF1) localizes in the cytosol under normal growing conditions (Figure 8A and B).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 8A and B.

claim: With Parkin translocation after 3 hr of valinomycin treatment, GFP-mRABGEF1 is robustly recruited to the mitochondria.
source: With Parkin translocation after 3 hr of valinomycin treatment, GFP-mRABGEF1 is also robustly recruited to the mitochondria (Figure 8A and B).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 8A and B.

claim: RABGEF1 recruitment to mitochondria requires both Parkin expression and loss of membrane potential.
source: RABGEF1 recruitment to mitochondria requires both Parkin expression and loss of membrane potential (Figure 8—figure supplement 1A) and was observed both in WT and TBC1D15/17 DKO cells with similar efficiencies (Figure 8—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1A.

claim: When introducing Y26A/A58D mutations to disrupt ubiquitin-binding ability, the translocation of RABGEF1 was completely blocked.
source: When introducing Y26A/A58D mutations to disrupt ubiquitin-binding ability (described later and [Lee et al., 2006; Penengo et al., 2006]), the translocation of RABGEF1 was completely blocked (Figure 8A and C), strongly suggesting that RABGEF1 binds to poly-ubiquitin chains that Parkin builds on damaged mitochondria.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 8A and C.

claim: RABGEF1 binds to poly-ubiquitin chains that Parkin builds on damaged mitochondria.
source: When introducing Y26A/A58D mutations to disrupt ubiquitin-binding ability (described later and [Lee et al., 2006; Penengo et al., 2006]), the translocation of RABGEF1 was completely blocked (Figure 8A and C), strongly suggesting that RABGEF1 binds to poly-ubiquitin chains that Parkin builds on damaged mitochondria.
evidence: This is inferred from the mutant analysis in Figure 8A and C.

claim: Knocking down of the downstream Rab-related factors including MON1, CCZ1, and RAB7A did not affect the mitochondrial recruitment of RABGEF1.
source: Consistent with this, knocking down of the downstream Rab-related factors including MON1, CCZ1, and RAB7A did not affect the mitochondrial recruitment of RABGEF1 (Figure 8—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 2.

claim: GST-mRABGEF1 WT efficiently pulled down 2× and higher ubiquitin chains.
source: Recombinant linear tandem (1×, 2×, 3×, and 4×) ubiquitins (Figure 8—figure supplement 3B) were incubated with GST-mRABGEF1. GST-mRABGEF1 WT efficiently pulled down 2 × and higher ubiquitin chains (Figure 8D and E).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 8D and E.

claim: When single mutations, Y26A or A58D, were introduced, the amounts of eluted ubiquitin were slightly reduced compared to WT.
source: When single mutations, Y26A or A58D, were introduced, the amounts of eluted ubiquitin were slightly reduced compared to WT (Figure 8D and E).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 8D and E.

claim: The double mutation Y26A/A58D completely lost the ability to bind ubiquitin.
source: In sharp contrast, the double mutation Y26A/A58D completely lost the ability to bind ubiquitin (Figure 8D and E).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 8D and E.

claim: The overall binding profiles of RABGEF1 to phosphorylated ubiquitin were quite similar to those of non-phosphorylated ubiquitin.
source: The binding ability to phosphorylated ubiquitin, which was produced by incubating with recombinant TcPINK1 (Figure 8—figure supplement 3C) was also tested. The overall binding profiles were quite similar to those of non-phosphorylated ubiquitin (Figure 8D and E).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 8D and E.

claim: RABGEF1 WT, and single Y26A and A58D mutants could bind both K48- and K63-linked ubiquitin or phosphorylated ubiquitin chains.
source: RABGEF1 WT, and single Y26A and A58D mutants could bind both K48- and K63-linked ubiquitin or phosphorylated ubiquitin chains, but Y26A/A58D mutant completely did not (Figure 8F).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 8F.

claim: Y26A/A58D mutant completely did not bind K48- and K63-linked ubiquitin or phosphorylated ubiquitin chains.
source: RABGEF1 WT, and single Y26A and A58D mutants could bind both K48- and K63-linked ubiquitin or phosphorylated ubiquitin chains, but Y26A/A58D mutant completely did not (Figure 8F).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 8F.

claim: Mouse RABGEF1 UBD interacts with monomeric non-phosphorylated ubiquitin with a dissociation constant of 2.2 μM.
source: ITC showed that mouse RABGEF1 UBD interacts with monomeric non-phosphorylated and phosphorylated ubiquitin with a dissociation constant of 2.2 μM and 5.6 μM, respectively (Figure 8G, and Figure 8—figure supplement 3D and E).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 8G.

claim: Mouse RABGEF1 UBD interacts with monomeric phosphorylated ubiquitin with a dissociation constant of 5.6 μM.
source: ITC showed that mouse RABGEF1 UBD interacts with monomeric non-phosphorylated and phosphorylated ubiquitin with a dissociation constant of 2.2 μM and 5.6 μM, respectively (Figure 8G, and Figure 8—figure supplement 3D and E).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 8G.

claim: Neither ubiquitin-chain linkage nor S65 phosphorylation substantially affect the binding affinity between ubiquitin and RABGEF1.
source: All these biochemical results strongly suggest that neither ubiquitin-chain linkage nor S65 phosphorylation substantially affect the binding affinity between ubiquitin and RABGEF1.
evidence: This is concluded from the biochemical data in Figure 8D-G.

claim: RABGEF1-mAID, but not WT RABGEF1, was degraded within 16 hr of indolacetic acid (IAA) treatment.
source: RABGEF1-mAID, but not WT RABGEF1, was degraded within 16 hr of indolacetic acid (IAA) treatment (Figure 9A), a half-life that is much shorter than conventional siRNA methods.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 9A.

claim: The efficiency of Parkin translocation did not change after RABGEF1 degradation.
source: The efficiency of Parkin translocation (Figure 9B) and MFN2 degradation (Figure 9C) did not change after RABGEF1 degradation.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 9B.

claim: MFN2 degradation did not change after RABGEF1 degradation.
source: The efficiency of Parkin translocation (Figure 9B) and MFN2 degradation (Figure 9C) did not change after RABGEF1 degradation.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 9C.

claim: TOMM20 and MT-CO2 degradation was slightly inhibited in RABGEF1-mAID cells when compared to WT cells.
source: However, TOMM20 and MT-CO2 degradation was slightly inhibited in RABGEF1-mAID cells when compared to WT cells (Figure 9C).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 9C.

claim: A substantial fluorescent shift of mt-mKeima occurred by 6 hr of OAQ treatment in WT cells, which was impaired in RABGEF1-mAID cells.
source: We found a substantial fluorescent shift by 6 hr of OAQ (oligomycin and antimycin A) treatment in WT cells, which was impaired in RABGEF1-mAID cells (Figure 9D and E).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 9D and E.

claim: RABGEF1 is important for efficient elimination of damaged mitochondria through autophagy.
source: These results strongly suggest that RABGEF1 is important for efficient elimination of damaged mitochondria through autophagy.
evidence: This is concluded from the mitophagy assays in Figure 9.

claim: Overexpressed TBC1D15 and TBC1D17 localize in cytosol.
source: As previously reported, overexpressed TBC1D15 and TBC1D17 localize in cytosol, but FIS1 overexpression direct them to the mitochondria (Figure 10A).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 10A.

claim: FIS1 overexpression directs TBC1D15 and TBC1D17 to the mitochondria.
source: As previously reported, overexpressed TBC1D15 and TBC1D17 localize in cytosol, but FIS1 overexpression direct them to the mitochondria (Figure 10A).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 10A.

claim: None of the endosomal Rab knock-down abrogated mitochondrial localization of TBC1D15.
source: In control siRNA-treated cells, endogenous TBC1D15 was colocalized with TOMM20, and none of the endosomal Rab knock-down abrogated mitochondrial localization of TBC1D15 (Figure 10B), strongly suggesting that mitochondrial localization of TBC1D15 (and TBC1D17) depends on FIS1, but not endosomal Rabs and their related factors.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 10B.

claim: Mitochondrial localization of TBC1D15 (and TBC1D17) depends on FIS1, but not endosomal Rabs and their related factors.
source: In control siRNA-treated cells, endogenous TBC1D15 was colocalized with TOMM20, and none of the endosomal Rab knock-down abrogated mitochondrial localization of TBC1D15 (Figure 10B), strongly suggesting that mitochondrial localization of TBC1D15 (and TBC1D17) depends on FIS1, but not endosomal Rabs and their related factors.
evidence: This is concluded from the siRNA experiments in Figure 10B.

claim: Core regulators of vesicle transport system in the endosomal Rab cascade have an ability to associate with mitochondria during their engulfment by autophagosomes.
source: However, in this study, we found that core regulators of vesicle transport system in the endosomal Rab cascade have an ability to associate with mitochondria during their engulfment by autophagosomes (Figure 11).
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study shown in the model in Figure 11.

claim: The sequential Rab cascade on damaged mitochondrial membranes is in the same order as that occurring during endocytosis.
source: Therefore, the sequential Rab cascade on damaged mitochondrial membranes is in the same order as that occurring during endocytosis.
evidence: This is concluded from the experiments showing RABGEF1, RAB5, MON1/CCZ1, and RAB7A recruitment.

claim: RABGEF1 is recruited to damaged mitochondria in a UBD-dependent manner.
source: Moreover, RABGEF1, the most upstream GEF for the endosomal Rab cascade, recognizes mitochondrial damage though the UBD (Figure 11).
evidence: This is demonstrated through the Y26A/A58D mutant experiments in Figure 8.

claim: Mitochondrial RABGEF1 is a platform for transfer of the signal to the downstream Rab cascade.
source: In this study, we identified that RABGEF1 is recruited to damaged mitochondria in a UBD-dependent manner, and found that mitochondrial RABGEF1 is a platform for transfer of the signal to the downstream Rab cascade.
evidence: This is concluded from the experiments showing RABGEF1 recruitment and its role in RAB5 recruitment.

claim: RAB7A directs ATG9A vesicles to damaged mitochondria and/or facilitates the assembly of ATG9A vesicles near damaged mitochondria during Parkin-mediated mitophagy.
source: siRNA-based experiment strongly suggests that RAB7A directs ATG9A vesicles to damaged mitochondria and/or facilitates the assembly of ATG9A vesicles near damaged mitochondria during Parkin-mediated mitophagy.
evidence: This is concluded from the RAB7A knockdown experiments in Figure 3.

claim: When excess amounts of RAB7A are recruited to damaged mitochondria by deletion of mitochondrial Rab-GAPs, an excess amount of ATG9A vesicles is also recruited along with LC3-labeled autophagic membranes.
source: Moreover, when excess amounts of RAB7A are recruited to damaged mitochondria by deletion of mitochondrial Rab -GAPs, an excess amount of ATG9A vesicles is also recruited along with LC3-labeled autophagic membranes.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4B and C.

claim: Mitochondria-targeted RAB7A likely regulates ATG9A vesicle trafficking during mitophagy.
source: Considering the correlation between the amount of RAB7A associated to the damaged mitochondria and the efficiency of ATG9A recruitment, mitochondria-targeted RAB7A likely regulates ATG9A vesicle trafficking during mitophagy (Figure 11).
evidence: This is inferred from the correlation observed in the experiments.

claim: ATG9A localizes to different membrane compartments such as TGN, recycling membrane and plasma membrane.
source: Indeed, ATG9A localizes to different membrane compartments such as TGN, recycling membrane and plasma membrane, whose trafficking as well as autophagosome formation under starvation conditions are regulated by several Rab proteins (RAB1 and RAB11) and their regulators (TBC1D5, TBC1D14, and TRAPPIII complex) (Lamb et al., 2016; Longatti et al., 2012; Popovic and Dikic, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations.

claim: RAB7A is a new mitophagy-specific ATG9A vesicle regulator.
source: Here, we identified RAB7A as a new mitophagy-specific ATG9A vesicle regulator.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the study.

claim: ATG9A might be required not only qualitatively but also quantitatively for expanding LC3-labeled membrane structures.
source: ATG9A might be required not only qualitatively but also quantitatively for expanding LC3-labeled membrane structures.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the observations.

claim: RAB7A on mitochondria may facilitate the expansion of phagophore by assisting fusion of ATG9A vesicles with the phagophore.
source: Given that Rab proteins function in membrane fusion, RAB7A on mitochondria may facilitate the expansion of phagophore by assisting fusion of ATG9A vesicles with the phagophore.
evidence: This is a speculation based on known Rab protein functions.

claim: Upon Parkin-mediated mitophagy, RAB7A regulates coordinated action of making precise autophagosome between LC3-labeled preautophagosome membrane and ATG9A vesicles.
source: We, therefore, propose that upon Parkin-mediated mitophagy, RAB7A regulates coordinated action of making precise autophagosome between LC3-labeled preautophagosome membrane and ATG9A vesicles.
evidence: This is the proposed model from the study.

claim: Mitochondria represent an off target site for RAB7A.
source: The fact that RAB7A appears on the mitochondrial surface more so in TBC1D15/17 DKO cells may reflect that mitochondria represent an off target site for RAB7A and that the mitochondrial RAB7-GAPs dissociate RAB7A so it may target adjacent phagophore membranes.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the observations in knockout cells.

claim: The mitochondrial RAB7-GAPs dissociate RAB7A so it may target adjacent phagophore membranes.
source: The fact that RAB7A appears on the mitochondrial surface more so in TBC1D15/17 DKO cells may reflect that mitochondria represent an off target site for RAB7A and that the mitochondrial RAB7-GAPs dissociate RAB7A so it may target adjacent phagophore membranes.
evidence: This is a speculation about the function of mitochondrial RAB7-GAPs.

claim: RAB5 on the mitochondria recruits RAB7A to this site where it is dissociated by TBC1D15/17, perhaps to target local growing phagophores and augment their growth around mitochondria.
source: RAB5, on the other hand, appears targeted directly to the OMM by RABGEF1 via binding ubiquitin chains catalyzed there by Parkin. One scenario is that RAB5 on the mitochondria recruits RAB7A to this site where it is dissociated by TBC1D15/17, perhaps to target local growing phagophores and augment their growth around mitochondria.
evidence: This is a proposed scenario based on the experimental findings.

claim: A similar Rab pathway may exist to expand phagophore around pathogens.
source: As OPTN and NDP52 initiate phagophore recruitment to invading bacteria, it is tempting to suggest that a similar Rab pathway may exist to expand phagophore around pathogens.
evidence: This is a speculation about potential parallels with xenophagy.

claim: RAB7A is recruited to the growing phagophore during xenophagy.
source: RAB7A is also recruited to the growing phagophore during xenophagy (Yamaguchi et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citation.

claim: Phagophore expansion regulated by RAB7A might be a shared molecular hub between mitophagy and xenophagy that relays ubiquitin signaling to the endomembrane system for autophagosome assembly.
source: Therefore, phagophore expansion regulated by RAB7A might be a shared molecular hub between mitophagy and xenophagy that relays ubiquitin signaling to the endomembrane system for autophagosome assembly.
evidence: This is a speculation about shared mechanisms between mitophagy and xenophagy.
